claims.text: GNP per person divides a national aggregate by population, so unequal distribution can leave many households with low incomes despite a high average. Unrecorded household farming and informal sales can make measured output incomplete. Money income does not show whether people can obtain safe water, education or health care. It also leaves out losses such as damaged habitats and the value of unpaid care. Price differences change what a given income buys, so international comparisons need a comparable basis. An average may help compare economic resources, but combine it with evidence on distribution, services and environmental conditions before judging living standards.
